prompt:
Build a differential tracked ground vehicle with a rigid chassis, two independently driven tracks, finite track inertia, and nonlinear frictional contact with the terrain. Drive forces must reach the chassis through the two track-terrain contact paths; directly prescribing chassis motion is not a valid implementation.

Read left_track_command, right_track_command, payload_mass, terrain_friction, grade_angle, left_traction_loss, and traction_event_time from base-workspace variables. Their nominal values are 1.45 m/s, 1.45 m/s, 300 kg, 0.72, 3 deg, 0.35, and 5.4 s. They operate respectively over 0.70--2.10 m/s, 0.70--2.10 m/s, 120--520 kg, 0.48--0.95, -6--9 deg, 0--0.58, and 4.2--7.0 s. The left-track friction coefficient is reduced by left_traction_loss for 1.2 s beginning at traction_event_time; zero means no traction reduction.

Assume a clean MATLAB session in which only the declared public inputs are provided. Use a 720 kg base chassis and a 1.2 m track-centre spacing. A reduced planar longitudinal-yaw chassis model is intended: no independent lateral-velocity state is required, and chassis translational velocity is aligned with the reported yaw direction. Across the declared range, regulate actual left and right track motion, produce the corresponding forward and differential-steering response through physical contact forces, remain dynamically bounded, and recover after the temporary traction loss.

Log Timeseries vehicle_motion, track_state, terrain_contact, and drive_actuation. vehicle_motion must contain [x position in m, y position in m, yaw angle in rad, chassis forward speed in m/s, yaw rate in rad/s]. track_state must contain [actual left and right track surface speeds in m/s, left and right contact slip ratios]. For each side, define slip as (track surface speed minus the local chassis path speed) divided by max(abs(track surface speed),abs(local chassis path speed),0.35 m/s); the local path speeds use the stated 1.2 m track-centre spacing. terrain_contact must contain [left and right longitudinal interface forces in N, left and right positive normal-load magnitudes in N]. The longitudinal channels may consistently report either terrain-on-vehicle forces or their equal-and-opposite vehicle-on-terrain reactions, but one global convention must be used for both sides and every run. drive_actuation must contain the actual bounded left and right generalized drive forces in N under one fixed global actuator sign convention. The logged quantities must come from the causal driven vehicle and contact simulation rather than from commands or precomputed trajectories.

Work directly in the required model file and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XMECH01.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
